about:
Hi! I am Bryan, an Economics PhD student at Nanyang Technological University (NTU) in Singapore. I'm interested in international trade such as why prices move, how trade flows shift, and how politics changes both.

Before pursuing my PhD, I spent two years at S&P Global as a price assessment specialist, covering movements in commodity prices. I spoke with traders and producers across Asia every day and wrote daily reports explaining the movements of prices. Earlier, I worked in strategy and market research at Kantar Consulting, Jacaranda Capital Partners and FairPrice Group.

I graduated with a Bachelor of Business (Banking and Finance, specialising in International Trade) and a Masters of Science (International Political Economy), both from NTU as well. 

In my spare time, I like to exercise (although life has kept me busy in recent months). I love drinking coffee and tea, although I wouldn't say I'm a caffeine aficionado (coffee shop is good enough). Sometimes, I teach economics and business to students in Junior College and University.

Here, I share my thoughts and opinions regarding economic matters, and teach those who are unfamiliar with certain topics happening globally.
